_design: ViT-tiny, CIFAR-100 @10%, ONE shared baseline. The only thing that varies across arms is which information source was fused in, so any difference in WHAT they fix is attributable to the source.

_predictions_recorded_before_running.same_currency_pair: prior|simclr -- these tie end-to-end (29.74 vs 29.77), have near-equal feature gain (14.85 vs 13.46), and their combination is neutral (29.93). If 'same currency' is real, they should fix OVERLAPPING images and learn SIMILAR representations: fixed-similarity and CKA-similarity HIGH.
_predictions_recorded_before_running.different_currency_pair: prior|augmentation -- these STACK (the prior's gain grows 1.6x under DeiT augmentation). If 'different currency' is real, they should fix DIFFERENT images: fixed-similarity and CKA-similarity LOWER than the same-currency pair.
_predictions_recorded_before_running.band: S(prior,simclr) - S(prior,augmentation) > 0 on the fixed-set measure. No magnitude is predicted; the measure is new and has no prior scale.
_predictions_recorded_before_running.falsifier: S(prior,augmentation) >= S(prior,simclr) => 'same currency' does not show up in WHICH images are fixed or WHICH representations are learned, and the taxonomy's mechanism rests on the equality of G magnitudes alone. That would have to be said in the paper.
